brief.meaningEn: The overall feeling and small distinctive details of an experience.
brief.meaningZh: 一段經歷的整體感受和令它顯得鮮明的細節。
brief.grammar: Tone suggests emotional quality; texture suggests varied lived details. Both are figurative here.
brief.register: Reflective descriptions of daily life, places and stories.
brief.boundaryZh: 不要把日常生活的 tone 當成電話鈴聲，或把 texture 限於物件的表面觸感。
brief.misconceptionZh: 這組詞描述感受與細節，不保證生活一定愉快。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出哪些小選擇改變了整體感受，以及哪些細節因此變得鮮明。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 82, row 10; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: Small choices give daily life its tone and texture.

options.en: It made the week feel warmer through repeated stories and meals.
options.zh: 反覆分享故事和一起吃飯，令一星期感覺更溫暖。

options.en: It solved all of the family’s problems at once.
options.zh: 它一下子解決了一家人的所有問題。

options.en: It changed only the sound of the dining-room bell.
options.zh: 它只改變了飯廳鈴聲。

options.en: It made Friday meals unfamiliar and less personal.
options.zh: 它令星期五的晚餐變得陌生而欠缺個人色彩。

listening.explanationZh: 故事與熟悉菜式改變了整體感受和生活細節，並非解決所有問題。
listening.en: A family began eating dinner together on Fridays. The meal did not solve every problem, but the shared stories and familiar recipes gave the week a warmer tone and texture.
listening.zh: 一家人開始在星期五一起吃晚飯。這頓飯並沒有解決所有問題，但大家分享的故事和熟悉的菜式，令一星期多了溫暖的氛圍和細節。

reply.promptZh: （星期五的晚餐怎樣影響這家人的一星期？）

options.en: It gave them a warmer shared routine.
options.zh: 它給了他們較溫暖的共同習慣。

options.en: Their stories added personal detail to the week.
options.zh: 他們的故事為一星期添上個人色彩。

options.en: It gave the week a warmer tone and texture.
options.zh: 它令一星期更有溫暖的氛圍和生活細節。

options.en: Familiar food made their time together feel different.
options.zh: 熟悉的食物令相聚時間有了不同感受。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都描述共同晚餐帶來的感受和細節。
reply.promptEn: How did the Friday meal affect the family’s week?

scene.promptZh: 一間社區圖書館在閱讀角加入居民手寫薦書卡，訪客因而感到更親切，也發現各人的閱讀趣味。哪句最貼切？

options.en: The notes give the reading corner a more personal tone and texture.
options.zh: 這些薦書卡令閱讀角更有親切的氛圍和個人細節。

options.en: The notes make the corner look personal, but visitors never read or notice them.
options.zh: 薦書卡令閱讀角看似有個人色彩，但訪客從未閱讀或留意它們。

options.en: The cards list books, but they do not show anything about the residents’ reading choices.
options.zh: 卡片列出書名，卻沒有展示居民的閱讀喜好。

scene.explanationZh: 手寫薦書卡同時改變閱讀角的感受，並展示各人的趣味。

contrast.promptZh: 哪句誤把 texture 只理解成物件表面？

options.en: Shared habits can shape the feel of a week.
options.zh: 共同習慣可以改變一星期的感受。

options.en: The phrase refers only to whether the dinner table feels rough or smooth.
options.zh: 這組詞只指飯桌表面是粗糙還是光滑。

options.en: Small details can make a place feel distinctive.
options.zh: 細節可以令一個地方更鮮明。

contrast.explanationZh: 這裏的 texture 是生活細節的比喻，並非桌面的觸感。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友問：「薦書卡只是紙張，真的會改變閱讀角嗎？」你知道訪客讀了卡片後更願意交流。哪句最完整？

options.en: The cards change the corner’s tone and texture: handwritten choices make it feel welcoming and give visitors details to discuss.
options.zh: 薦書卡改變了閱讀角的氛圍和細節：手寫選書令它更親切，也給訪客交流的話題。

options.en: The cards are handwritten.
options.zh: 卡片是手寫的。

options.en: Visitors have something to read.
options.zh: 訪客有東西可讀。

dialogue.explanationZh: 金句同時交代整體感受和具體細節。

speaking.en: Handwritten recommendations gave the library corner a friendly tone and texture.
speaking.zh: 手寫薦書卡令圖書館的閱讀角更有親切氛圍和鮮明細節。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說出哪項細節令閱讀角感覺不同。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：長者中心把原本冷清的等候區改成小型植物角，並讓會員輪流寫植物照顧提示。用一至兩句英文描述這些選擇如何改變等候經驗。
writing.selfCheckZh: 指出整體感受和一項具體細節；不要聲稱等候時間因此縮短。

examples.en: The plants and members’ care notes gave the waiting room a gentler tone and texture, although the appointment times stayed the same.
examples.zh: 植物和會員寫的照顧提示令等候區氣氛更柔和，也添上生活細節，但預約時間沒有改變。

examples.en: A rotating set of care notes gave the room a personal tone and texture, while the plants welcomed waiting visitors.
examples.zh: 輪流更新的照顧提示令房間更有個人氛圍與細節；植物則令等候訪客感到受歡迎。

glossary.en: A rotating set of care notes

takeaways.en: The music changed the café’s tone and texture without changing its menu.
takeaways.zh: 音樂沒有改變咖啡店的餐牌，卻改變了店內的氛圍和細節。

takeaways.en: Small shared habits can give ordinary days a distinctive tone and texture.
takeaways.zh: 共同的小習慣可令平凡日子有鮮明的氛圍與細節。

notes: AI-authored provisional proposal; independent English, Chinese, media and browser QA remain pending.

brief.meaningEn: The uncomfortable sense that someone else is directing one’s choices too closely.
brief.meaningZh: 覺得別人過分主導自己的選擇而感到不自在。
brief.grammar: Being managed is a passive -ing clause after the feeling of; the concern is perceived control, not necessarily the helper’s intention.
brief.register: Family, work and education discussions about autonomy.
brief.boundaryZh: 即使建議出於好意，對方仍可能覺得選擇被接管；不應反推對方完全拒絕幫助。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要把這句誤解成單純不喜歡安排時間，也不要假定所有指引都不受歡迎。
brief.outcomeZh: 能說明哪個決定被別人代做，以及怎樣保留當事人的選擇權。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 84, row 5; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: Teenagers often resist the feeling of being managed.

listening.promptZh: 美娜為何提出自己選活動？

options.en: She wanted some control over her own weekend choices.
options.zh: 她想對自己的週末選擇保留一些決定權。

options.en: She disliked every activity her father suggested.
options.zh: 她不喜歡父親建議的所有活動。

options.en: Her father had not made any suggestions.
options.zh: 她父親完全沒有提出建議。

options.en: She wanted someone else to decide all the activities.
options.zh: 她希望由別人決定所有活動。

listening.explanationZh: 她接受建議，但想保留部分選擇權。
listening.en: Mina’s father chose every activity for her weekend. She liked his suggestions, but resisted the feeling of being managed and asked to choose one activity herself.
listening.zh: 美娜的父親替她選好週末的每項活動。她喜歡父親的建議，卻不喜歡被別人管着的感覺，於是提出自己選一項活動。

reply.promptZh: （美娜為何要求自己選一項活動？）

options.en: She wanted a say in the weekend plan.
options.zh: 她想對週末計劃有發言權。

options.en: She resisted the feeling of being managed.
options.zh: 她不喜歡被別人管着的感覺。

options.en: She preferred to choose something herself.
options.zh: 她寧願自己作出部分選擇。

options.en: She liked the suggestions but wanted more autonomy.
options.zh: 她喜歡那些建議，但想有更多自主權。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都說明她想保留決定權，而非拒絕所有建議。
reply.promptEn: Why did Mina ask to pick one activity?

scene.promptZh: 一位員工願意聽取主管意見，但主管每天改寫她的工作清單，連先後次序也不讓她決定。哪句最貼切？

options.en: She appreciates advice but dislikes the feeling of being managed.
options.zh: 她感激意見，卻不喜歡被別人管着的感覺。

options.en: She appreciates advice, so she must welcome the daily rewriting of her task list.
options.zh: 她感激意見，所以必定歡迎每天有人改寫她的工作清單。

options.en: She wants to set task priorities, so she must reject every suggestion from the manager.
options.zh: 她想決定工作先後，所以必定拒絕主管的所有建議。

scene.explanationZh: 接受建議與不願被接管每個決定可以同時成立。

contrast.promptZh: 哪句把不喜歡被管着誤解為拒絕一切幫助？

options.en: A person may welcome options while choosing for themselves.
options.zh: 一個人可以歡迎別人提供選項，同時自己作決定。

options.en: If she dislikes being managed, she must refuse every suggestion.
options.zh: 她若不喜歡被人管着，就一定拒絕所有建議。

options.en: Being consulted can make a plan feel more collaborative.
options.zh: 得到徵詢可令計劃更像共同商議。

contrast.explanationZh: 不喜歡選擇被接管，不等於拒絕所有建議。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「我只是幫她排好所有工作，她為何不高興？」你知道對方想自己決定先後次序。哪句最完整？

options.en: She may value your advice but dislike the feeling of being managed; offer priorities as options and let her choose the order.
options.zh: 她可能重視你的意見，卻不喜歡被別人管着的感覺；你可以提供工作優先次序作參考，讓她自己決定先後。

options.en: She wants a different order.
options.zh: 她想用另一個次序。

options.en: Your advice may be useful.
options.zh: 你的意見可能有用。

dialogue.explanationZh: 金句承認好意，並給予保留選擇權的做法。

speaking.en: She liked the suggestions but resisted the feeling of being managed.
speaking.zh: 她喜歡那些建議，卻不喜歡被別人管着的感覺。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出「接受建議」與「自己決定」如何並存。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：社區計劃顧問替居民選好花園設計；居民願意看草圖，但希望自行投票決定最後方案。用一至兩句英文說明居民的感受與要求。
writing.selfCheckZh: 說明居民並非拒絕草圖，而是希望保留最後選擇權。

examples.en: Residents welcomed the design sketches but disliked the feeling of being managed, so they asked to vote on the final garden plan.
examples.zh: 居民歡迎設計草圖，卻不喜歡被別人管着的感覺，因此要求就最後的花園方案投票。

examples.en: The consultant’s drawings were useful, yet the feeling of being managed remained until residents were offered a final vote.
examples.zh: 顧問的圖則有用，但居民仍有被別人管着的感覺，直到他們獲得最後投票的機會。

takeaways.en: A learner may like useful feedback yet dislike the feeling of being managed.
takeaways.zh: 學習者可能喜歡有用的意見，卻不喜歡被別人管着的感覺。

takeaways.en: Giving people a choice can reduce the feeling of being managed.
takeaways.zh: 給予人們選擇權，可以減少被別人管着的感覺。

notes: AI-authored provisional proposal; independent English, Chinese, media and browser QA remain pending.

lessons.titleEn: build a world out of words

brief.meaningEn: Create a vivid imagined setting through writing rather than physical construction.
brief.meaningZh: 以寫作塑造鮮明的想像場景，而不是實際建造地方。
brief.grammar: Build and out of form a creative-construction metaphor; words are the writer’s material.
brief.register: Literary discussion, storytelling and creative writing.
brief.boundaryZh: 鮮明世界需要場景、人物與細節相互配合；並非只要堆砌華麗字詞便能做到。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要把 world 當成真正建成的地方，亦不要說沒有圖畫就不能想像場景。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出文字中的具體線索如何令讀者想像一個地方。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 89, row 2; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: A skilled writer can build a world out of words.
sources.expression: build a world out of words

listening.promptZh: 作者如何令讀者想像街市？

options.en: She used sensory details to make the setting vivid.
options.zh: 她用感官細節令場景鮮明。

options.en: She built a real market before writing the story.
options.zh: 她先建造真正的街市才寫故事。

options.en: She avoided describing sounds, places and smells.
options.zh: 她避免描寫聲音、地方和氣味。

options.en: She relied on a map rather than any words.
options.zh: 她只靠地圖，沒有用文字。

listening.explanationZh: 聲音、石級與麵包等文字細節令場景具體。
listening.en: In a short story, the writer described the market’s closing calls, wet stone steps and warm bread from a corner stall. With those details, she built a world out of words that readers could picture.
listening.zh: 在短篇故事裏，作者描寫街市收檔的叫賣聲、濕漉漉的石級，以及街角攤檔的熱麵包。藉着這些細節，她用文字建構了一個讀者能想像的世界。

reply.promptZh: （作者用街市細節達到了甚麼效果？）

options.en: She helped readers picture the market.
options.zh: 她幫讀者想像街市。

options.en: She gave the setting sounds and physical details.
options.zh: 她讓場景有聲音和具體細節。

options.en: She built a world out of words.
options.zh: 她用文字建構了一個世界。

options.en: She made a fictional place feel present to readers.
options.zh: 她令虛構地方彷彿呈現在讀者眼前。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都說明文字如何令想像場景變得鮮明。
reply.promptEn: What did the writer achieve with the market details?

scene.promptZh: 學生寫一段關於山村的故事，提到霧中的石橋、清晨的鐘聲和屋裏的炭火，讀者因此彷彿身在村中。哪句最貼切？

options.en: The student built a world out of words by giving the village vivid details.
options.zh: 學生以鮮明細節用文字建構了一個山村世界。

options.en: The student listed the bridge and bell, but readers still learned nothing about the village atmosphere.
options.zh: 學生提到石橋和鐘聲，但讀者仍完全無法感受山村氣氛。

options.en: The story describes the village clearly, but only a photograph could make readers imagine it.
options.zh: 故事清楚描寫山村，但只有照片才能令讀者想像它。

scene.explanationZh: 文字細節足以令讀者想像山村，毋須實際建造或依賴照片。

contrast.promptZh: 哪句把 build 誤解為實際建造？

options.en: A few well-chosen details can make a setting vivid.
options.zh: 幾個恰當細節可以令場景鮮明。

options.en: The author must put up real buildings before readers can imagine the village.
options.zh: 作者必須先建起真正的房屋，讀者才能想像山村。

options.en: Readers can picture a place through sound and smell descriptions.
options.zh: 讀者可從聲音和氣味的描寫想像地方。

contrast.explanationZh: 這裏的 build 是創作比喻，不是實際建築。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「故事沒有插圖，讀者怎會看見那個山村？」你讀到石橋、鐘聲和炭火的描寫。哪句最完整？

options.en: The bridge, bell and hearth let the author build a world out of words, giving readers enough clues to picture the village without illustrations.
options.zh: 石橋、鐘聲和爐火讓作者用文字建構一個世界，提供足夠線索，讓讀者不用插圖也能想像山村。

options.en: The story mentions a bridge.
options.zh: 故事提到一座橋。

options.en: Illustrations are not essential.
options.zh: 插圖並非必不可少。

dialogue.explanationZh: 金句把文字細節與讀者形成畫面的過程連起來。

speaking.en: With the market’s sounds and smells, she built a world out of words.
speaking.zh: 透過街市的聲音和氣味，她用文字建構了一個世界。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出哪兩種感官細節讓場景變得鮮明。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：少年寫一篇海底研究站的科幻故事，描述窗外的藍光、儀器的低鳴和狹窄走廊。用一至兩句英文介紹這些細節如何幫助讀者想像場景。
writing.selfCheckZh: 至少指出兩項文字細節和讀者如何想像研究站；不要寫成少年真的建造了研究站。

examples.en: The young writer built a world out of words with blue light beyond the windows and the low hum of instruments inside the station.
examples.zh: 少年作者用窗外的藍光和站內儀器的低鳴，以文字建構海底研究站的世界。

examples.en: The writer built a world out of words with a narrow corridor and the glow outside, letting readers picture life beneath the sea.
examples.zh: 作者以狹窄走廊和窗外的光用文字建構一個世界，讓讀者想像海底生活。

takeaways.en: Choosing details readers can sense helps a novelist build a world out of words.
takeaways.zh: 小說家可選擇讀者能感受到的細節，用文字建構一個世界。

takeaways.en: The place existed only on the page, but the writer built a world out of words that felt real.
takeaways.zh: 那個地方只存在於書頁上，但作者用文字建構出彷彿真實的世界。

notes: AI-authored provisional proposal; independent English, Chinese, media and browser QA remain pending.
